subject: Using Genomic SEM to perform LDSC

messages.author: 90589675ea303876
messages.subject: Using Genomic SEM to perform LDSC
parts:
Hi, Michel and Andrew,  I am using Genomic SEM to obtain LDSC to examine the correlation between my GWAS -by- subtraction outputs and other published GWAS as per Demange et al . The current output gives me the following:
Mean Z*Z: 0.3004
Cross trait Intercept: 0.1037(0.008)
cov_g: 0.0451 ( 0.0035 )

Is There extra code I need to use to calculate the genetic correlation and p value

Kind regards Joan

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: Using Genomic SEM to perform LDSC
parts:
hi,
have a look at the github for that paper Perline Demange put together, it has a large section on correlations with other traits, and two ways of actually computing those:

https://github.com/PerlineDemange/non-cognitive/tree/master/GenomicSEM/Genetic%20correlations

let me know if you have any questions after looking over those scripts etc. 

Best,
Michel

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Using Genomic SEM to perform LDSC
parts:
Hi Joan, 

It sounds like you were both asking for more information on conducting GWAS-by-subtraction, but also just how to get the genetic correlation results for a pair of traits. I just made some edits to the ldsc function so that it will now print genetic correlation results at the end of the .log file. If you reinstall Genomic SEM, restart R, and re-run ldsc that will give you those results. Alternatively, you can also run cov2cor on the genetic covariance matrix output from ldsc, but if you want the standard error you'll have to rerun ldsc. 

-Andrew
